text:
The Maple Leafs won in Boston on Friday, and it barely changed the conversation. They're 10-14-3, 2-7-1 in their last ten, with a 5% playoff chance by our simulations, and the headlines are about everything except the standings: the Rangers reportedly preparing a pitch for Auston Matthews if he wants out, William Nylander saying "I didn't agree with it" about his drop to the second power-play unit (TSN's headline), and Jim Hiller's handling of rookie Gavin McKenna.

The underlying numbers say this is a flawed team, not just an unlucky one. Toronto has 47% of the expected goals (the quality of chances on both sides) and has scored nearly seven more goals than its chances. The net has been the disaster: Sergei Bobrovsky is .827 over his last five starts, all losses, 7.6 goals worse than expected, and Kirill Marchenko made headlines for what he said about him. Nylander is running cold too, four points in ten games on 9.6 expected.

There are pieces. Matthews with Jack Roslovic and Easton Cowan has an 11-4 goal edge, and with Kirill Marchenko, now back from injured reserve, in Cowan's spot that line has had 67% of the chances in a small sample. Morgan Rielly scored his 100th goal Friday. Chris Tanev left that game with a lower-body injury. Watch Anthony Stolarz's grip on the net, and Matthews.
